plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like flowers that brighten the winter landscape. Hundreds of cultivars exist with single, semi-double, and fully double forms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early spring (peak in midwinter in mild climates)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and China; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, Mediterranean Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative, is the plant from which all true tea is made.

plants.name: Hamamelis mollis
plants.description: A deciduous large shrub that flowers on bare branches in the depths of winter. Its spidery, ribbon-like petals are strongly fragrant and tolerate frost by curling up in the cold.
plants.location: Native to central and eastern China; grown in temperate gardens across Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Witch hazel petals curl up tightly during freezing weather to protect themselves and unfurl again when it warms.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking shrub with huge, artichoke-like flower heads made of colorful bracts surrounding a central cone of tiny flowers. It is adapted to fire-prone fynbos habitats and is the national flower of South Africa.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer, with blooms from late spring through summer (peaking around December to February in some areas)
plants.location: Native to the Western and Eastern Cape of South Africa; cultivated in Australia, Hawaii, and California
plants.funFact: Proteas are among the most ancient flowering plants, with a lineage dating back roughly 300 million years, and the genus is named after the shape-shifting Greek god Proteus.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A broad, umbrella-shaped tree that becomes covered in clusters of brilliant flowers during the Southern Hemisphere summer. Its feathery, fern-like leaves provide dappled shade.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere (December to February); also blooms in dry season in some tropical areas
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; widely planted in Australia, Brazil, the Caribbean, and tropical Africa
plants.funFact: Despite being a popular tree around the world, the royal poinciana is endangered in its native Madagascar.
